title: Three Shifts and One Short Rope
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：reward　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 reward 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the foreman ① offered the reward that no worker in the site would have recorded, and he said the offering was the whole of the shift. The ② reward, meaning the prize itself and not the rope, ran three shifts and stayed unrecorded in the book; a reward, he said, is the only thing in a site that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ reward in that site had the same short rope beside it, and the ④ reward at the far ramp, meaning the load they kept for the children to lift and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A reward, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the foreman said the recording is the part that fills three shifts.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the reward was the whole of the matter, meaning the thanks and not the prize. The ⑥ reward, meaning the thanks and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; reward, he said, is either something you offer or the only word that means both a prize and a thanks. He said the thanks is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ reward had become a line in a sheet, and the sheet had become an argument about the short rope. The ⑧ reward of the whole thing, the foreman wrote in May, was one site and three shifts of recording; reward, he said, is either the load at the far ramp or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ reward I remember is the prize recorded in the sheet, which closed in 1974 and is still recorded as the quietest in the site. A ⑩ reward, my mother said in 1976, is the only prize that improves by being recorded; every reward, she said, is a thanks that has agreed to look like a prize. She said the thanks was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 报酬；奖励（指工地里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 报酬；奖励（指那份报酬本身，与短短的绳索相对）
C. 固定搭配：offer the reward 给这一份报酬
D. n. 报酬；奖励（指留给孩子们抬的那一车）
E. n. 报酬之事（抽象总称，指一处工地的报酬之事）
F. n. 报酬；奖励（指施工单里写到、被记载的那一份）
G. n. 报酬、谢意（指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 谢意（抽象总称，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: offered the reward that no worker in the site would have recorded
The reward, meaning the prize itself and not the rope
the reward at the far ramp
the reward was the whole of the matter
the reward had become a line in a sheet
The reward of the whole thing
A reward, my mother said in 1976

answers.why: offer the reward 意为“给这一份报酬”，1967 年那位工头把工地里没有一位工人肯记载的一份报酬做了一遍。
reward 意为“报酬；奖励”，指那份报酬本身而不是短短的绳索，它经过了三个班次而在簿子上没有被记载。
reward 意为“报酬；奖励”，指工地里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一根短短的绳索。
reward 意为“报酬；奖励”，指最远那道坡台的留给孩子们抬的那一车，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
reward 意为“报酬、谢意”，指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份谢意就是那件事的全部。
reward 意为“谢意”，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份报酬，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
reward 意为“报酬；奖励”，指施工单里写到、被记载的那一份，到 1972 年这一份成了施工单里的一行。
reward 意为“报酬之事”，工头五月写道，整件事的报酬之事是一处工地和三个班次的记载。
reward 意为“报酬；奖励”，我记得的是施工单里记载过的那一份，1974 年收工了，至今仍被说成工地里最安静的一份。
reward 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，报酬是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的报酬。

那份报酬，指的是那份报酬本身而不是短短的绳索，经过了三个班次而在簿子上没有被记载。（reward）
